items.text: The team has decided to design a new remote control that is original, trendy, and user-friendly.
The remote control should be multi-functional, capable of controlling not just TV but also household devices like air conditioners and heating systems.
The remote control should be compact and have a friendly, trendy design, such as a kidney shape or different colors and materials.
The remote control should beep when a user claps to help prevent loss and improve usability.
Eileen and S3 will try out the whiteboard and see if they can draw a cat or rabbit to demonstrate how the remote control might look.
S2 will draw a snake as part of the design exploration.
Team members are to take individual work on functional, conceptual, and detailed design phases, followed by group discussion.
Team members are to make notes on the design requirements, including originality, usability, and functionality.
S3 will consider redesigning the remote control after the initial design phase is complete.
Team members are to think about the production cost, aiming for less than 1250 euros per unit, and a selling price of 25 euros with a profit target of 50 million euros.
Team members are to identify and share their experiences or frustrations with current remote controls during the meeting.
Can the remote control be designed to be used for multiple household functions beyond TV?
Implement a feature that emits a beep or signal when the remote control is clapped or when it detects being in a dark spot (e.g., covered by a newspaper or behind a plant).
Include a light sensor that activates a light or beep signal when the remote is in a dark environment, such as behind a plant or under a sweater.
Develop a working design that incorporates both voice and clap-based activation, though these are considered less reliable and not sufficient on their own.
The remote control should have a sensor to detect darkness and respond with a signal (light or beep) when hidden or covered.
The next meeting will be in 30 minutes, and participants will receive notices via computer.
The industrial designer is responsible for the working design, while the marketing manager will develop user requirement specifications (e.g., friendliness, usability, price).
The price of the remote control must be justified by sufficient features to ensure market competitiveness.
The team will work on a functional design that includes user-friendly features such as voice or clap response, but with limitations acknowledged.
Participants will receive specific instructions for the working and functional design phases.
The team will meet again in 30 minutes to review progress and discuss outcomes.
What specific trigger (clap, voice, light sensor) should be used to activate the remote's signal when lost or hidden?
How can the remote be reliably found in dark or hidden locations without relying solely on voice or clap commands?
